summary: Moore County, NC, tower listed as erected in 1944 at 120 feet. A 2018 article names an Eagle Springs tower as still operated; no current status found.

facts.status_note: A 2018 Pinestraw Magazine article names an Eagle Springs tower among three still operated; it does not say whether that is this tower, and no source confirms its condition since.
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Forest Lookouts lists a 120-foot tower erected at Eagle Springs; no design or builder given.
Pinestraw article, page dated August 2018, quotes a Scotland County ranger naming one of three still-operated towers as Eagle Springs.

evidence.supports: Eagle Springs lookout listed in Moore County under the NC Division of Forest Resources
evidence.quote: Moore County - North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

evidence.supports: speaker is a Scotland County ranger
nearly all state towers decommissioned; three still operated, one in Eagle Springs
evidence.quote: nearly all the 100 fire lookout towers across the state have been decommissioned. We still operate three: the one here, one in Eagle Springs and one in Hamlet.

evidence.supports: article names Eagle Springs as a tower location without giving a county

notes_for_editor: Dated facts rest on one line each: a 1944 build entry on the Forest Lookouts list (no citation given there) and one quoted remark in a Pinestraw feature. The feature's page shows August 2018 and says the Hamlet tower was last active in 2013, so it postdates 2013. The article does not say its Eagle Springs tower is the Moore County tower on the Forest Lookouts list; the story flags this. Two web searches found nothing else about this tower. The brief's unknown status is kept; no corrections to the brief.
